_readme: Coverage map for arXiv:1902.08184v4 -- 'Stability conditions in families',
Bayer, Lahoz, Macri, Nuer, Perry, Stellari. Created for destination issue
#198 under epic #190 (stability-families).
THIS IS NOT A TRUST RECORD AND NOT A MINT SURFACE. It is a zero-claim map
of the paper's structure onto statuses. formalization.yaml's `source`
remains the Bridgeland 2007 record, and registry/bridgeland2007.json
remains the only mint surface; nothing in this file changes either, and
nothing in this file may be cited as theorem coverage. The only status
that ever counts as coverage is 'formalized'. A 'mapped' entry remains a
candidate correspondence and makes no coverage claim.
Validation: python scripts/check_coverage_map.py
Run it before and after every edit to this file. It fails on any status
outside the vocabulary, any non-target status without complete evidence,
and any corpus-derived identifier key.
Update ownership: the owner (Chris Dare) promotes statuses; agents may
propose a promotion only by PR carrying the evidence fields the validator
demands, and 'formalized' additionally requires explicit owner acceptance
recorded in the entry. Adding sections, fixing titles against the pinned
PDF, and adding tracking links are ordinary edits; status promotion is
not.
Quotes: none are minted here. When a quote is later needed it must be
checked directly against the v4 artifact identified in `source` -- never
against the arXMCP corpus, whose rows carry no arXiv version (see
`corpus_note`).

near_term_coordinates.note: Weak stability conditions and HRS tilting. The repository holds abstract HRS-tilt machinery and source-facing candidates for Definitions 14.1--14.12, display (14.1), Proposition 14.16, and Lemma 14.17. The exact charge Z/(i-beta), support transport, noetherian zero-charge torsion conclusion, and the separate Hom-vanishing refinement are implemented. CLOSEOUT REVIEW 2026-08-14: the type-two classification predicate stores phase-cut membership and the positive-new-imaginary Hom implication, whereas the printed Lemma 14.17 states Hom vanishing as a subsequent moreover conclusion. The current biconditional is therefore a strengthened candidate, not a literal source binding. Issue #208 and epic #192 remain open; this coordinate stays mapped and must not be promoted.

evidence.v4_check: Pages 71--74 were checked directly against the pinned v4 PDF. The display (14.1) cutoff conventions, Definition 14.12 envelope, and Proposition 14.16 charge normalization match the source-facing adapters. Lemma 14.17 does not yet have a literal biconditional because the Lean type-two predicate includes an additional Hom-vanishing implication. The mapped status records this candidate and explicit mismatch; it is not a reviewed coverage claim.

near_term_coordinates.note: Uniform quadratic support across a family. PROMOTED target -> mapped 2026-08-11: Support/Quadratic.lean supplies a genuine bundled QuadraticForm and its implication to the norm support predicate; Support/Uniform.lean forces one form across an indexed family; Support/ZeroChargeLattice.lean constructs the saturated subgroup generated by zero classes; Support/Quotient.lean puts the descended charge and one form on the real quotient; and the weak adapter binds the predicate to actual weak-semistable heart classes. UPDATE 2026-08-15: Support/Semistable.lean binds ordinary loci to actual slicing phases (#380). Support/IntegralRealQuotient.lean constructs the canonical integral-to-real scalar-extension comparison and requires explicit bijectivity before producing an equivalence (#387). Families/FiberwiseSupport.lean maps the K-groups and actual slicing-defined loci of varying abstract fiber categories into one common numerical space controlled by one charge and quadratic form (#389). Families/BaseChange.lean adds an abstract contravariant category-valued family, triangulated pullbacks, and compatible common class maps (#393). Families/PreStabilityBaseChange.lean packages actual pre-stability conditions on those fibers, requires an explicit preimage-slicing witness for every pullback, and proves phase, class, charge, and nonzero semistable-locus transport (#395). This is still a numerical candidate: the quotient comparison's bijectivity is model-specific, and no family of schemes, geometrically constructed derived pullback or preimage witness, relative category, HN geometry, boundedness, or moduli functor is supplied. The coordinate is therefore not reviewed or formalized.

evidence.v4_check: Read directly from the pinned v4 PDF on 2026-08-11. Page 87: Definition 18.5 fixes a Mukai homomorphism and says a (weak) HN structure satisfies support with respect to a quadratic form Q when its torsion-heart stability data does; Lemma 18.6 identifies this with the same Q on every fiber. Page 101: Definition 21.9 forms the saturated zero-class subgroup Lambda_0 and the free quotient Lambda/Lambda_0. Page 102: Definition 21.15(4) places Q on the real quotient, requires negativity on the descended kernel and nonnegativity on every fiber semistable class; clause (5) is boundedness and remains outside this mapping.

near_term_coordinates.note: TARGET UPDATED 2026-08-15: Families/Basic.lean isolates candidate interfaces for locally constant charge, openness, ordinary and weak HN integration after caller-designated Dedekind base changes, and boundedness. Families/Ordinary.lean combines Definition 20.5(1)-(3) with Definition 21.15(4)-(5) using quotient-uniform support. Families/FiberwiseOrdinary.lean removes the arbitrary-locus freedom from that ordinary adapter: actual slicings on varying abstract fiber categories supply the semistable classes, one common charge is compatible with every fiber, and projections recover both the five-clause package and exactly the four source clauses used by Theorem 22.2 (#391). Its PUnit model is inhabited. Families/BaseChange.lean organizes those fibers as a contravariant functor over an abstract base category, requires triangulated pullbacks, induces coherent K₀ pullback, and records common-class-map compatibility (#393). Families/PreStabilityBaseChange.lean binds actual fiber pre-stability conditions to those pullbacks using explicit Slicing.PreimageData witnesses; it proves phase, class, charge, and nonzero semistable-locus transport and supplies a constant model (#395). Families/CategoricalOrdinary.lean combines that pullback compatibility with the five-clause ordinary package, projects the four Theorem 22.2 source clauses, transports actual semistable classes and their common charge, and supplies a constant categorical model (#397). Families/Scheme.lean introduces actual scheme-valued base changes through Over S and realizes the charge, open-locus, and generic-semistability probes on schemes with their Zariski topology (#399). Families/ResidueFiber.lean constructs the actual residue-field base change Spec kappa(x) -> S and its canonical map to T, then evaluates the supplied triangulated family and K₀ pullback at that point fiber (#401). Families/SchemeDerived.lean constructs the unbounded and bounded derived categories of O_X-module sheaves on every scheme and residue-field scheme and records objectwise realization interfaces (#403). Families/ExactPullback.lean exposes actual additive module-sheaf pullback, its identity and composition isomorphisms, and the triangulated derived and K0 functors induced when that pullback is explicitly exact (#405). Families/ExactPullbackCoherence.lean proves that exact pullback is closed under identities and composition, lifts the unit and composition isomorphisms to cochain complexes, and makes the corresponding derived pullback functors available (#407). Families/DerivedPullbackCoherence.lean descends the unit and compositor through derived localization and proves identity and composition for the induced K0 pullbacks (#414). Families/DerivedPullbackLaws.lean proves the complex- and derived-level left-unit, right-unit, and associativity laws, using canonical congruence lifted through localization (#417). Families/DerivedPullbackShift.lean proves that the localization comparison and the complex, localized, and derived unit/compositor commute with integer shift (#425). Families/FlatPullback.lean proves that ordinary module pullback is automatically right exact, reduces exactness to finite-limit preservation, factors out the local-ring-valued presheaf-module stalk functor, proves it left exact on sheaves and invariant under module sheafification, proves the flat stalkwise scalar-extension model left exact, proves that module stalks jointly detect isomorphisms, and promotes pointwise finite-limit preservation to module sheaves globally. It also types the exact pullback-to-stalk comparison datum, proves that flatness plus that datum gives exact pullback, and makes the datum canonical for identities and closed under composition (#429). Families/OpenImmersionPullback.lean discharges the comparison directly through Mathlib restriction theorems and proves exact module-sheaf and derived pullback for every open immersion. Families/Weak.lean remains a fixed-category weak adapter. Families/Theorem22.lean records every missing geometric dependency and proves no manifold conclusion. Governance keeps this coordinate at target pending adversarial review and owner acceptance. The repository now has scheme-valued base changes, Zariski probes, concrete residue-field point indexing, actual objectwise derived categories of all module sheaves, exact derived pullback under a visible hypothesis and unconditionally for open immersions, and identity/composition functoriality and coherent unit/associativity laws through derived localization and K0, including shift-compatible unit and compositor. Only the presheaf module-pullback comparison with scalar extension on stalks is still missing from the exactness criterion, so there is not yet a general geometric instance from `[Flat f.left]` to `IsExactPullback f`. General nonexact left-derived pullback, bounded coherent or perfect derived subcategories, geometric preimage/HN witnesses, geometric openness theorem, relative HN construction, bounded moduli family, complex-manifold structure, proof of Theorem 22.2, and the later Section 23 results also remain open.
